pumac-2018-finals-b-01.prompt: Let a positive integer $n$ have at least four positive divisors. Let the least four positive divisors be $1=d_1<d_2<d_3<d_4$. Find, with proof, all solutions to $n^2=d_1^3+d_2^3+d_4^3$.
pumac-2018-finals-b-01.answer: There are no solutions (reduce mod $d_2$, then mod $q^2$ for the prime $q$ dividing $d_4$).

pumac-2018-finals-b-02.prompt: Aumann, Bill, and Charlie each roll a fair 6-sided die with sides labeled 1 through 6 and look at their individual rolls. Each flips a fair coin and, depending on the outcome, looks at the roll of either the player to his right or the person to his left, without anyone else knowing which die he observed. Then, at the same time, each of the three players states the expected value of the sum of the rolls based on the information he has. After hearing what everyone said, the three players again state the expected value of the sum of the rolls based on the information they have. Then, for the third time, after hearing what everyone said, the three players again state the expected value of the sum of the rolls based on the information they have. Prove that Aumann, Bill, and Charlie say the same number the third time.
pumac-2018-finals-b-02.answer: All three say $a+b+c$, the actual sum (case analysis on whether the first statements agree).

pumac-2018-finals-b-03.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle. Construct three circles $k_1,k_2$ and $k_3$ with the same radius such that they intersect each other at a common point $O$ inside the triangle $ABC$ and $k_1\cap k_2=\{A,O\}$, $k_2\cap k_3=\{B,O\}$, $k_3\cap k_1=\{C,O\}$. Let $t_a$ be a common tangent of circles $k_1$ and $k_2$ such that $A$ is closer to $t_a$ than $O$. Define $t_b$ and $t_c$ similarly. Those three tangents determine a triangle $MNP$ such that triangle $ABC$ is inside the triangle $MNP$. Prove that the area of $MNP$ is at least $9$ times the area of $ABC$.
pumac-2018-finals-b-03.answer: $[MNP]=\left(1+\frac Rr\right)^2[ABC]\ge9[ABC]$ for the triangle of centers (use Euler's inequality $R\ge2r$).
